title: Finite discrete coefficient realization reflects constructible finite-Tor objects
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme and A a finite discrete commutative ring. For the specified finiteComparisonRealization from fixed-scalar pro-etale sheaves to internal coefficient modules, any fixed-scalar complex whose realization is bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude is itself bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude. The internal condition is [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the derived category is [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the functor is the specified coefficient transport of [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing].

source.place: Opening coefficient-identification paragraph: exact coefficient equivalence preserves constructibility and finite Tor amplitude.

proof.text: Use finiteComparisonRealization_exact to install the exact coefficient equivalence. Its derived functor reflects canonical t-boundedness by the proved source lemma Functor.bounded_of_bounded_mapDerivedCategory_obj, applied to the boundedness component of the hypothesis.

A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the reverse direction of finiteComparisonGenerators_identification to obtain an etale bounded constructible finite-Tor complex L and an isomorphism from its ordinary pro-etale comparison image to K.

For each integer q, convert the constructibility of H^q(L) to Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf using isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf. Apply the proved source theorem isConstructible_comparisonUpperStar_obj. The exact-functor homology isomorphism followed by homology of the isomorphism to K identifies this comparison image with H^q(K); transport constructibility along that isomorphism.

Take a Tor interval [a,b] for L. The proved source theorem ProEtale.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory sends this same interval through ordinary comparison inverse image. Transport the resulting property along the isomorphism to K using ObjectProperty.prop_of_iso. Together with boundedness and cohomological constructibility this is the asserted conjunction.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient-identification paragraph, using the existing bounded finite-Tor generator identification and the proved ordinary-comparison preservation of constructibility and Tor intervals; no new coefficient tensor equivalence is needed.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteDiscreteCtfRealization
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (A : Type) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    (eR : Sheaf.sheafifyRingPresheaf.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (coherentTopology Profinite.{u})
      ((Functor.const Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ).obj (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} A))) ≅
        Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} A) [IsMonHom eR.hom]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A))))
    (hK : (constantModelBoundedConstructible (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj A) X ⊓
      fun M ↦ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ M)
        ((finiteComparisonRealization A X eR).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded K ∧
      ∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructible (ULift.{u + 1} A)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) ∧
      DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ K
